headline: Darren Thompson sees Australian small caps as positioned to reclaim underperformance relative to large caps, supported by valuations
reasoning: Thompson notes that domestically, it has been large caps — particularly banks and big resources — that have driven the Australian market, while small caps have materially underperformed. He attributes this partly to the structural shift toward passive investing and large super fund concentration in large caps. While acknowledging the headwind of a slowing economic environment for small caps, he believes valuations are supportive and that the large-cap dominance has largely played out, leaving room for small caps to recover.
quote: Small caps here have been left behind. So uh so it's an interesting dynamic. Small caps globally have really rallied domestically. It's been the large caps that have driven our market particularly in to date the banks and the resort. Big resources, small caps have really underperformed materially. Um, now they generally wouldn't do well in a slowing economic environment. So there's that headwind. However we do think valuations are supportive. I think partly the structure of our market has been a factor in that the the amount of active investor base has gone down a lot. So passive investing has, has, has, has a much larger part of our market. And then your future, your super test. And the big concentration in super funds means that buying a lot of the large caps have driven our market, and I think that that's largely played out. And so we do think that small caps probably have a place to reclaim some of that underperformance.
